newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF okays Nomura head's plan to resign from JSDA.
newsitem.headline: MOF okays Nomura head's plan to resign from JSDA.

text.p: The chairman of Nomura Securities Co Ltd Masashi Suzuki said on Monday that the Ministry of Finance had accepted his intention to resign as the head of the Japan Securities Dealers Association (JSDA).
Suzuki said he would publicly announce his intention to resign as chairman of the association later on Monday.

Nomura said last week that two of its directors were involved in suspected illegal deals in which substantial sums of Nomura money were moved to a corporate customer's account. Suzuki told reporters on Monday: "Due to the issue, which has recently caused a stir in Japanese society, I am not confident about working as the head of the (industry) institution and I also feel I will be unable to show leadership (in the industry)."
He also said he was planning to resign from a senior position at the Japan Federation of Economic Organisations (Keidanren), an influential business group.
Media reports have said that the corporate client is linked to a former "sokaiya" stocks racketeer but Nomura has said it could not confirm this.
